rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a proposal or offer that someone has put forward.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 tai4 ji5 gei2 kap1 jan5

rows.note: Use this when the offer is specifically a price or amount proposed in a sale or negotiation.

example.jyutping: nei5 go3 ceot1 gaa3 taai3 dai1 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for volunteering to do something or putting forward an idea, opinion, or suggestion.

example.english: I offer to look over the contract for you.
example.traditional: 我主動提出幫你睇份合約。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zyu2 dung6 tai4 ceot1 bong1 nei5 tai2 fan6 hap6 joek3

rows.note: Use this when making a thing, service, resource, or facility available for someone to use or consider.

example.english: This library will offer a free study room.
example.traditional: 呢間圖書館會提供免費自修室。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 tou4 syu1 gun2 wui5 tai4 gung1 min5 fai3 zi6 sau1 sat1

rows.note: Use this specifically when offering a price, reward, or amount of money in a bid.

example.english: They offer five hundred thousand for my shop.
example.traditional: 對方出價五十萬買我間舖。
example.jyutping: deoi3 fong1 ceot1 gaa3 ng5 sap6 maan6 maai5 ngo5 gaan1 pou3

rows.note: Use this in formal or religious contexts when presenting something to a god or as a sacrifice.

example.english: The worshippers offer fresh flowers to the god.
example.jyutping: seon3 zung3 hoeng3 san4 hin3 soeng6 sin1 faa1
